The double-sided size selection protocol outlined in this appendix is designed for the selection of library molecules (inclusive of adapter) in the range of 250 – 450 bp. To obtain a population of shorter or longer molecules, the protocol may be modified as follows: A B C D 1 Upper size limit Modification Lower size limit Modification 2 Increase Decrease the ratio of the first cut Increase Decrease the ratio of the second cut* 3 Decrease Increase the ratio of the first cut Decrease Increase the ratio of the second cut* * The second size cut should be performed with at least 0.2 volumes of KAPA cleanup beads reagent. Please note that the volume of KAPA cleanup beads needed for the second cut is calculated relative to the volume of the DNA at the start of the size selection procedure, not the volume of the DNA-containing supernatant transferred after the first cut. DNA recovery is dramatically reduced if the difference between first and second cuts is less than ~0.2 volumes. To increase the amount of DNA recovered, >0.2 volumes of KAPA cleanup beads may be used for the second cut, but note that this may result in the recovery of smaller library fragments and/or a broader size distribution. For more information on double-sided size selection, please refer to the KAPA NGS Library Preparation Technical Guide (available on request from Technical Support at sequencing.roche.com/support).

steps.title: Prepare DNA Samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the dsDNA for library construction based on the presence of EDTA.

substeps.instruction: If DNA contains EDTA: either perform a 3X bead-based cleanup with KAPA cleanup beads (refer to TDS KR1705 or KR1245) or prepare a diluted Conditioning Solution (5 µL per sample plus excess).
If DNA does not contain EDTA: dilute in 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0 – 8.5) to a total volume of 35 µL.
If DNA contains EDTA: dilute in the current EDTA-containing buffer to a total volume of 30 µL, then add 5 µL of diluted Conditioning Solution.
Mix by gentle vortexing or pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Enzymatic Fragmentation
steps.instruction: Assemble and incubate the fragmentation reaction on ice.

substeps.instruction: Assemble the reaction on ice: 35 μL dsDNA (with Conditioning Solution if needed), 5 μL KAPA Frag Buffer (10X), and 10 μL KAPA Frag Enzyme (Total volume: 50 μL). Note: Buffer and Enzyme may be pre-mixed.
Vortex gently, spin down briefly, and return to ice.
Incubate in a thermocycler pre-cooled to 4 °C. Set heated lid to ≤ 50 °C if used.
Run program: Pre-cool block at 4 °C, then Fragmentation at 37 °C (time per table), then HOLD at 4 °C.
Transfer reactions to ice immediately.

steps.title: End Repair and A-Tailing
steps.instruction: Perform end repair and A-tailing in the same tubes used for fragmentation.

substeps.instruction: Assemble reaction: 50 μL fragmented dsDNA, 7 μL End Repair & A-Tailing Buffer, and 3 μL HyperPrep or HyperPlus ERAT Enzyme Mix (Total volume: 60 μL). Note: Buffer and enzyme may be pre-mixed.
Vortex gently, spin down briefly, and return to ice.
Incubate in a thermocycler with a heated lid set to ~ 85 °C.
Run program: End repair and A-tailing at 65 °C for 30 min, then HOLD at 4 °C (or 20 °C if proceeding immediately to ligation).

steps.title: Adapter Ligation
steps.instruction: Dilute adapters and perform the ligation reaction.

substeps.instruction: Dilute adapter stocks according to the input DNA amount (e.g., 1 μg input: 15 μM stock; 1 ng input: 300 nM stock) as per Table 4.

Assemble reaction in the same tubes: 60 μL End repair/A-tailing product, 5 μL diluted adapter stock, 5 μL PCR-grade water, 30 μL Ligation Buffer, and 10 μL DNA Ligase (Total volume: 110 μL). Note: Water, buffer, and ligase may be pre-mixed.
Mix thoroughly and centrifuge briefly.
Incubate at 20 °C for 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours at 20 °C, or overnight at 2 °C to 8 °C for low-input samples).

steps.title: Post-Ligation Bead Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform a 0.8X bead-based cleanup to purify the ligated library.

substeps.instruction: Combine 110 μL ligation product with 88 μL KAPA cleanup beads (Total: 198 μL).
Mix thoroughly by vortexing or pipetting.
Incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes.
Place on magnet until liquid is clear.
Wash twice: add 200 µL 80% ethanol, incubate on magnet for ≥ 30 seconds, and discard ethanol.
Dry beads at room temperature for 3–5 minutes.
Remove from magnet and resuspend beads in elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0 – 8.5): use 25 µL for Library Amplification or 55 µL for double-sided size selection.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Place on magnet until liquid is clear.
Transfer supernatant to a new tube: 20 µL for Library Amplification or 50 µL for double-sided size selection.

steps.title: Library Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify the adapter-ligated library using PCR.

substeps.instruction: Assemble reaction: 25 μL KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix (2X), 5 μL Library Amplification Primer Mix (10X), and 20 μL adapter-ligated library (Total: 50 μL).
Mix thoroughly and centrifuge briefly.

Amplify using the following protocol: Initial denaturation 98 °C for 45 sec (1 cycle); Denaturation 98 °C for 15 sec, Annealing 60 °C for 30 sec, Extension 72 °C for 30 sec (multiple cycles); Final extension 72 °C for 1 min; HOLD at 4 °C.

steps.title: Post-Amplification Bead Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform a 1X bead-based cleanup of the amplified library.

substeps.instruction: Combine 50 μL amplification product with 50 μL KAPA cleanup beads (Total: 100 μL).
Mix thoroughly and incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes.
Place on magnet until liquid is clear.
Wash three times: add 200 µL 80% ethanol, incubate on magnet for ≥ 30 seconds, and discard ethanol.
Dry beads at room temperature for 3–5 minutes.
Remove from magnet and resuspend beads in elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0 – 8.5) or PCR-grade water (use 55 µL if proceeding to second cleanup or size selection).
Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Place on magnet until liquid is clear and transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Double-Sided Size Selection
steps.instruction: Perform two sequential bead-based cuts to select for DNA fragments between 250 bp and 450 bp.

substeps.instruction: First Cut (0.7X): Combine 50 μL DNA with 35 μL KAPA cleanup beads. Mix and incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes.
Place on magnet and carefully transfer ~ 80 µL of supernatant (fragments < 450 bp) to a new tube; discard beads.
Second Cut (0.9X): Combine 80 μL supernatant from first cut with 10 μL KAPA cleanup beads. Mix and incubate at room temperature for 5–15 minutes.
Place on magnet and discard the supernatant (fragments < 250 bp).
Wash beads twice: add 200 µL 80% ethanol, incubate on magnet for ≥ 30 seconds, and discard ethanol.
Dry beads at room temperature for 3–5 minutes.
Remove from magnet and resuspend beads in elution buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0 – 8.5).
Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes, place on magnet, and transfer the clear supernatant (size-selected DNA) to a new tube.
